summary: Aroostook County, ME: 1907 landowner station, 1921 steel tower; a 2017 windstorm took the cab, and the FFLA list still shows the tower standing without it.

facts.design: Guyed steel tower with an 8 by 8 foot wooden cab, reached by an open ladder
facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list shows the tower standing with its cab gone; a 2017 report says a windstorm took the cab. The register instead describes a radio repeater in the cab.

access.note: Access is with permit via private timber roads from the Dickey checkpoint.

visit.trail_note: The summit is reached only by trail.

events.note: Landowners built the first lookout. The register calls it a wood tower; a 1914 report says it was built of logs
Chief Warden Buck reports a wooden tower 20 feet high on the south bluff; a 1919 report says a log tower was built in 1917 on another bluff
Maine Forest Service steel tower with an 8 by 8 foot wooden cab. The register gives 54 feet; a 1920 inventory and a 1921 newspaper item give 48 feet
Maine Forest Service panorama map centered on the Rocky Mt. tower in Township 18 Range 12
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on November 24, 1995, nominated by Robert Spear of the FFLA
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 15, 2008
Chapter visit: the cab needs a new floor and likely roof work; no repair trip could be organized that year
Windstorm on October 30, 2017 blew the cab off the steel tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Unresolved: the register gives 54 feet, while a 1920 inventory and a 1921 newspaper item give 48 feet. No height_m is recorded.

Unresolved: the register and the 1914 report disagree on whether the 1907 station was wood or logs, and a 1919 report describes a log tower on another bluff in 1917 where a warden reported a wooden tower on the south bluff.
The FFLA list and the 2017 report agree the cab is gone. The register's repeater note has no date and is reported as stated, not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: Probably the same mountain as us-me-rocky-mountain-2 (National Historic Lookout Register point, FFLA list coordinates 47.19176, -69.28156). This record's FFLOS point (47.27678, -69.28333) is about 9 km further north; decide whether the two should be merged. The brief's status 'gone' conflicts with the FFLA list. Photos: the firetower.org page credits a repeater photo to the St. John Valley Amateur Radio Association, but no image URL was captured, so no photo entry. The register misspells the association as 'Amatuer', kept verbatim in the quote.
